newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks ease 0.4 pct on cash shortage.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks ease 0.4 pct on cash shortage.

text.p: Istanbul shares slipped lower on Thursday on lack of fresh cash entry which capped the index's upside after Wednesday's 1.48 percent rise, brokers said.

"Volume still remains low and the market does not look so attractive in the medium-term. It is likely to fluctuate in 62,000-64,000 range tomorrow and next week," said Barbaros Alten from Global Securities.

The IMKB-100 closed down 261.28 points, or 0.41 percent at 63,225.18 after falling from an early high of 63,826. Trade volume was slightly lower at 5.7 trillion lira ($65.3 million) after six trillion ($68.4 million) on Wednesday.
Brokers said the index moved in a very narrow range at above 63,000-point support after failing to pierce resistance at between 63,800-64,000.
The market had recovered part of its earlier losses yesterday after losing three percent in the first two days of the week because of the Iraqi tension.
